title: ImmunCHECKpoint-Inhibitor-Associated Cardio-Oncological Follow-Up Care Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Technologies
summary:
Modern medicines used to treat advanced skin cancer can greatly improve the chances of survival. However, in rare cases they may also affect the heart. At present, it is difficult to predict which patients are at increased risk of developing heart problems during treatment.
The aim of this study is to identify factors that can help detect heart problems at an early stage. In the future, these findings will be used to develop a tool that helps doctors identify patients at higher risk and provide more personalized follow-up care.
The study includes patients with skin cancer who are receiving this type of cancer treatment. Participants will be followed for twelve months. All medical examinations are part of their routine care. In addition, participants will receive a smartwatch and smartphone applications that collect information such as heart rate, physical activity, movement, and sleep. They will also regularly answer questions about their health and well-being. The collected information will be analyzed to identify patterns that may predict the development of heart problems.

interventions.name: Prospective, single-arm observational study of melanoma patients receiving treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a 12-month observation period. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Melanoma patients with stage IIB through IV prior to starting PD-1-based immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy
- Sufficient knowledge of German
- Histologically confirmed melanoma
- ECOG ≤ 1
- Completed and signed written informed consent form
- Life expectancy of ≥ 1 year
- Ownership of a smartphone
Exclusion criteria:
-  Pregnancy
-  Melanoma patients who are not receiving PD-1-based ICI therapy
- Life expectancy < 1 year
- ECOG ≥ 2
- Lack of capacity to give informed consent
